units.title: Inside the CPU
units.tip: The CPU (processor) is the brain of the computer. It contains cores that execute instructions, a clock that synchronizes operations, and caches that store frequently used data. Transistors are the tiny switches that make everything work. Different instruction sets like x86 and ARM define how programs are written.

exercises.question: What is a CPU core?
exercises.answer: An independent processing unit that executes instructions
exercises.explain: Each core can run its own instruction independently. A multi-core CPU can run multiple instructions at the same time, improving performance.
choices: An independent processing unit that executes instructions
The power supply of the CPU

exercises.question: What is the CPU clock?
exercises.answer: A pulse that synchronizes when the CPU executes instructions
exercises.explain: The clock sends pulses at regular intervals (measured in GHz). Each pulse allows the CPU to perform one or more operations. A faster clock means more pulses per second.
choices: A pulse that synchronizes when the CPU executes instructions
A timer that tells you the time

exercises.question: What is CPU cache?
exercises.answer: Ultra-fast memory that stores frequently accessed data
exercises.explain: Cache is much faster than RAM. The CPU stores data it needs frequently in cache (L1, L2, L3) to avoid slow trips to main memory.
choices: Ultra-fast memory that stores frequently accessed data

exercises.question: Why does a multi-core CPU help?
exercises.answer: It can work on several tasks at the same time
exercises.explain: Each core runs its own stream of instructions, so more cores let the computer do more things at once. It does not make any single core faster.
choices: It makes each core run hotter and faster
It replaces the need for RAM
It can work on several tasks at the same time

exercises.question: What do transistors do in a CPU?
exercises.answer: Act as tiny electronic switches that represent 0 and 1
exercises.explain: Transistors are the building blocks of computer logic. Billions of transistors switch on and off to perform calculations and store data.
choices: Act as tiny electronic switches that represent 0 and 1

exercises.question: What is an instruction set?
exercises.answer: The set of commands a CPU can directly execute
exercises.explain: An instruction set defines the basic operations a CPU understands. Programs are compiled or written for a specific instruction set.
choices: The set of commands a CPU can directly execute

exercises.question: What is the x86 instruction set?
exercises.answer: An instruction set used in most desktop and laptop computers
exercises.explain: x86 is the dominant instruction set for personal computers. It is used by Intel and AMD processors in most Windows and Linux computers.
choices: An instruction set used in most desktop and laptop computers

exercises.question: What is the ARM instruction set?
exercises.answer: An instruction set used in phones, tablets, and some laptops
exercises.explain: ARM is energy-efficient and dominates mobile devices. It is used in iPhones, Android phones, and increasingly in personal computers.
choices: An instruction set used in phones, tablets, and some laptops

exercises.question: Why can a program built for x86 not run directly on an ARM chip?
exercises.answer: The two use different instruction sets, so the machine code does not match
exercises.explain: Programs are compiled into machine code for one instruction set. x86 code is not valid ARM code, so the program must be rebuilt for ARM or run through translation.
choices: The two use different instruction sets, so the machine code does not match
x86 programs are always too large

exercises.question: What advantage does ARM have over x86?
exercises.answer: Lower power consumption, making it ideal for mobile devices
exercises.explain: ARM designs are typically simpler and use less power. This is why phones and tablets use ARM; longer battery life matters for portable devices.
choices: Lower power consumption, making it ideal for mobile devices
ARM runs every x86 program unchanged

units.title: Memory and Storage
units.tip: RAM is fast temporary memory that your computer uses while running programs. Storage (SSD or HDD) holds data permanently. SSDs are faster but more expensive. HDDs are slower but cheaper and hold more data. NVMe is a fast storage interface used by many SSDs.

exercises.question: Why do computers need both RAM and storage?
exercises.answer: RAM is fast but temporary; storage is slower but permanent
exercises.explain: RAM lets programs run at speed but loses data on shutdown. Storage keeps data safe long-term. Both are needed for a working computer.
choices: RAM is fast but temporary; storage is slower but permanent

exercises.question: What happens to data in RAM when you turn off the computer?
exercises.answer: It is erased because RAM needs continuous power
exercises.explain: RAM is volatile memory. Without power, the electrical charges holding the data disappear. This is why you save files to storage.
choices: It is erased because RAM needs continuous power
It waits for the next boot

exercises.question: What is the relationship between RAM size and multitasking?
exercises.answer: More RAM lets you run more programs smoothly at once
exercises.explain: RAM holds the active programs and data. More RAM means more programs and data can be held simultaneously without slowdowns.
choices: More RAM lets you run more programs smoothly at once

exercises.question: What is VRAM?
exercises.answer: Memory on a graphics card used by the GPU
exercises.explain: VRAM (Video RAM) is dedicated memory on a graphics card. The GPU uses VRAM to store textures, images, and computational data for rendering.
choices: Memory on a graphics card used by the GPU

exercises.question: How do you know if your computer needs more RAM?
exercises.answer: Slowdowns, freezes, or constant disk activity when multitasking
exercises.explain: When RAM is full, the OS swaps data to disk (slow). Signs include lag, freezing, or your disk being constantly busy. More RAM fixes this.
choices: Slowdowns, freezes, or constant disk activity when multitasking

exercises.question: What is NVMe?
exercises.answer: A fast storage interface that connects directly to the motherboard
exercises.explain: NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) is much faster than older SATA connections. It uses the PCIe bus for higher speed and lower latency.
choices: A fast storage interface that connects directly to the motherboard

exercises.question: What is the difference between volatile and non-volatile memory?
exercises.answer: Volatile loses data without power; non-volatile keeps it
exercises.explain: Volatile memory (RAM) requires power to hold data. Non-volatile storage (SSD, HDD) keeps data without power.
choices: Volatile loses data without power; non-volatile keeps it
Non-volatile is the same as RAM

exercises.question: What does the capacity of a drive measure?
exercises.answer: How much data it can hold
exercises.explain: Capacity is the amount of data a drive can store, measured in gigabytes or terabytes. Speed is a separate property.
choices: How much data it can hold

exercises.question: What is a solid-state drive (SSD)?
exercises.answer: Storage using flash memory with no moving parts
exercises.explain: SSDs use flash memory chips like USB drives. They are fast, reliable, and have no moving parts, unlike HDDs.
choices: A drive that is solid metal
Storage using flash memory with no moving parts
The same as a hard drive

exercises.question: Why are HDDs still used despite being slower than SSDs?
exercises.answer: They are cheaper and can hold more data
exercises.explain: Mechanical hard drives cost less per gigabyte and can reach multi-terabyte capacities. For large storage on a budget, HDDs make sense.
choices: They are cheaper and can hold more data

units.title: Motherboards and Buses
units.tip: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects everything. The chipset controls data flow between components. Buses like PCIe and USB carry data between devices. BIOS/UEFI firmware initializes the hardware before the operating system starts.

exercises.question: What does a chipset do on a motherboard?
exercises.answer: Controls data flow between the CPU, RAM, storage, and peripherals
exercises.explain: The chipset is the traffic controller. It manages communication between the CPU and all other components like storage, USB, and network adapters.
choices: Controls data flow between the CPU, RAM, storage, and peripherals

exercises.question: What are the two main chipset brands?
exercises.answer: Intel and AMD (one for each CPU brand)
exercises.explain: Intel makes chipsets for Intel CPUs. AMD makes chipsets for AMD CPUs. The CPU and chipset must be compatible.
choices: Intel and AMD (one for each CPU brand)

exercises.question: What is a motherboard socket?
exercises.answer: The slot where the CPU plugs into the motherboard
exercises.explain: The socket holds the CPU and connects it to the motherboard. Different CPUs require different sockets, so compatibility matters.
choices: The slot where the CPU plugs into the motherboard

exercises.question: What is a DIMM slot on a motherboard?
exercises.answer: The slot where RAM modules plug in
exercises.explain: DIMMs (Dual Inline Memory Modules) are RAM sticks. Multiple DIMM slots let you add or upgrade RAM.
choices: The slot where RAM modules plug in

exercises.question: Why is compatibility between motherboard and CPU important?
exercises.answer: The socket must match or the CPU will not fit or work
exercises.explain: Different CPUs have different socket designs. An Intel CPU will not fit in an AMD socket and vice versa.
choices: The socket must match or the CPU will not fit or work

exercises.question: What is PCIe?
exercises.answer: A fast bus that connects graphics cards, storage, and other peripherals
exercises.explain: PCIe (PCI Express) is the standard way to connect expansion cards. It is much faster than older standards and comes in different versions.
choices: A fast bus that connects graphics cards, storage, and other peripherals

exercises.question: What is USB?
exercises.answer: A standard for connecting external devices like mice, keyboards, and drives
exercises.explain: USB (Universal Serial Bus) is the standard way to plug in peripherals. It is on every modern computer and provides power and data transfer.
choices: A standard for connecting external devices like mice, keyboards, and drives

exercises.question: What is BIOS?
exercises.answer: Firmware that initializes hardware before the OS boots
exercises.explain: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) runs before the OS. It checks hardware, loads settings, and starts the operating system.
choices: Firmware that initializes hardware before the OS boots

exercises.question: What is UEFI?
exercises.answer: Modern firmware that replaces BIOS with more features and security
exercises.explain: UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) is the successor to BIOS. It is faster, more secure, and supports larger drives.
choices: Modern firmware that replaces BIOS with more features and security

exercises.question: What is the role of the power supply in delivering power to components?
exercises.answer: Convert AC power to DC and distribute correct voltages to each component
exercises.explain: The PSU takes wall power (AC) and converts it to DC voltages (12V, 5V, 3.3V). Each component gets the right voltage.
choices: Convert AC power to DC and distribute correct voltages to each component
It stores energy like a battery

units.title: Graphics and Displays
units.tip: A graphics processing unit (GPU) specializes in rendering images and video. VRAM is the memory the GPU uses. Display resolution is the number of pixels. Refresh rate is how often the image updates per second.

exercises.question: What is a GPU?
exercises.answer: A processor specialized for rendering graphics and images
exercises.explain: GPUs have thousands of small cores for parallel processing. They are much faster at graphics than CPUs but specialized for that task.
choices: A processor specialized for rendering graphics and images

exercises.question: What is VRAM on a graphics card?
exercises.answer: Fast memory on the GPU for storing images and textures
exercises.explain: VRAM is dedicated memory attached to the GPU. Games and graphics-heavy programs store textures, meshes, and framebuffers in VRAM.
choices: Fast memory on the GPU for storing images and textures

exercises.question: What happens when a game needs more VRAM than the card has?
exercises.answer: Performance drops as data moves to slower memory
exercises.explain: When VRAM fills up, textures have to be swapped in and out of slower system memory. That causes stutter and lower frame rates.
choices: Performance drops as data moves to slower memory

exercises.question: Can a computer work without a dedicated graphics card?
exercises.answer: Yes, if the CPU has integrated graphics
exercises.explain: Many CPUs include integrated graphics. They are slower than dedicated cards but sufficient for everyday tasks. Gaming requires more power.
choices: Yes, if the CPU has integrated graphics
Only Macs can work without one
No, you must have a dedicated card

exercises.question: What is ray tracing in graphics?
exercises.answer: A rendering technique that simulates realistic light and shadows
exercises.explain: Ray tracing calculates light paths to create realistic reflections, shadows, and lighting. It is much slower than simple rasterization.
choices: A rendering technique that simulates realistic light and shadows

exercises.question: What is the difference between IPS and TN display panels?
exercises.answer: IPS usually has better colors and viewing angles; TN was usually faster
exercises.explain: IPS (In-Plane Switching) shows accurate colors from wide angles. TN (Twisted Nematic) is an older type with narrower viewing angles that was typically faster.
choices: IPS usually has better colors and viewing angles; TN was usually faster

exercises.question: What is response time on a monitor?
exercises.answer: How fast a pixel can change colors
exercises.explain: Response time is measured in milliseconds. Lower is better for gaming. A 1ms monitor responds faster than a 5ms monitor.
choices: How fast a pixel can change colors

exercises.question: What does HDR mean on a monitor?
exercises.answer: High Dynamic Range, showing brighter highlights and darker shadows
exercises.explain: HDR displays can show a wider range of brightness levels. This creates more contrast and realistic images.
choices: High Dynamic Range, showing brighter highlights and darker shadows

exercises.question: Why might a gamer prefer a 144Hz monitor over 60Hz?
exercises.answer: More refresh cycles per second means smoother motion
exercises.explain: A 144Hz monitor redraws the image 144 times per second instead of 60. This looks smoother, giving a competitive advantage in fast games.
choices: More refresh cycles per second means smoother motion

exercises.question: What is color accuracy on a monitor?
exercises.answer: How closely the monitor displays true colors
exercises.explain: A monitor with high color accuracy shows colors exactly as intended. This matters for photo editing and design work.
choices: How closely the monitor displays true colors

units.title: Power and Cooling
units.tip: The power supply provides the correct voltage and current to every component. Heat is generated by CPUs and GPUs, and cooling systems prevent overheating. Thermal throttling slows the CPU when it overheats to protect itself. Heat sinks and fans manage temperature.

exercises.question: What does a power supply (PSU) do?
exercises.answer: Convert AC wall power to DC voltages for computer components
exercises.explain: The PSU takes alternating current (AC) from the wall and converts it to direct current (DC) at various voltages like 12V, 5V, and 3.3V.
choices: Convert AC wall power to DC voltages for computer components

exercises.question: What is wattage in a power supply?
exercises.answer: The maximum power output the PSU can supply
exercises.explain: Wattage is measured in watts. A 650W PSU can supply up to 650 watts. You need enough wattage for all components plus overhead.
choices: The physical size of the PSU
The maximum power output the PSU can supply

exercises.question: What happens if a power supply is undersized?
exercises.answer: The computer may crash or shut down unexpectedly
exercises.explain: An undersized PSU cannot deliver enough power, causing instability, unexpected shutdowns, and potential hardware damage.
choices: The computer may crash or shut down unexpectedly

exercises.question: What is the 80+ certification on a PSU?
exercises.answer: A rating showing the PSU converts 80% or more of power efficiently
exercises.explain: 80+ Bronze/Gold/Platinum indicate efficiency levels. A higher rating means less wasted power as heat and lower electric bills.
choices: A rating showing the PSU converts 80% or more of power efficiently

exercises.question: How do you calculate total power needed for a build?
exercises.answer: Add the power of CPU, GPU, and other components, then add some headroom
exercises.explain: Sum the power draw of the major components, then pick a PSU with some extra capacity (often 20 to 30 percent) for stability and longevity.
choices: Add the power of CPU, GPU, and other components, then add some headroom
CPU power is all that matters

exercises.question: What is a heat sink?
exercises.answer: Metal fins that dissipate heat from the CPU or GPU to the air
exercises.explain: Heat sinks are typically made of aluminum or copper. They have large surface area to release heat from components to the surrounding air.
choices: Metal fins that dissipate heat from the CPU or GPU to the air

exercises.question: What is thermal paste?
exercises.answer: A conductive material between CPU and heat sink for better heat transfer
exercises.explain: Thermal paste fills microscopic gaps between the CPU and heat sink, improving contact and heat transfer efficiency.
choices: A conductive material between CPU and heat sink for better heat transfer

exercises.question: What is thermal throttling?
exercises.answer: Automatically slowing the CPU when it overheats
exercises.explain: Thermal throttling reduces CPU speed to lower heat generation and protect the hardware. It prevents damage but reduces performance.
choices: Automatically slowing the CPU when it overheats

exercises.question: What does a case fan do?
exercises.answer: Moves air through the case to carry heat out
exercises.explain: Fans push cool air in and hot air out, so heat from the CPU and GPU does not build up inside the case.
choices: Stores heat so the CPU stays cool
Moves air through the case to carry heat out
Absorbs electricity to cut power use

exercises.question: What is a good way to keep a computer cool?
exercises.answer: Ensure good airflow, clean dust, and maintain thermal paste
exercises.explain: Dust blocks cooling. Good case airflow, clean fans, and fresh thermal paste keep temperatures down. Liquid cooling is an option for extreme cases.
choices: Ensure good airflow, clean dust, and maintain thermal paste
Run the computer in the freezer

units.title: Building and Troubleshooting
units.tip: Building a computer requires checking compatibility: the motherboard socket must fit the CPU, RAM must fit DIMM slots, and the case must fit all components. POST (Power-on Self Test) happens at startup. Common failures include bad RAM, dead hard drives, and power supply issues.

exercises.question: What is the first step when building a computer?
exercises.answer: Check compatibility between motherboard, CPU, and RAM
exercises.explain: Before buying anything, verify socket compatibility (CPU to motherboard) and RAM type. Wrong combinations will not work at all.
choices: Check compatibility between motherboard, CPU, and RAM

exercises.question: What must you check before installing RAM?
exercises.answer: RAM type, speed, and number of slots on the motherboard
exercises.explain: Verify you have the right DDR generation (they are not interchangeable), a speed the board supports, and enough DIMM slots. The wrong type will not fit.
choices: RAM type, speed, and number of slots on the motherboard

exercises.question: What is an M.2 slot?
exercises.answer: A small slot on the motherboard for SSDs, commonly NVMe
exercises.explain: M.2 is a compact form factor for SSDs. Modern motherboards have one or more M.2 slots, and most carry fast NVMe drives.
choices: A small slot on the motherboard for SSDs, commonly NVMe

exercises.question: What is the case form factor?
exercises.answer: The size standard of the case (ATX, micro-ATX, mini-ITX)
exercises.explain: Form factors define case size. ATX is standard, micro-ATX is smaller, mini-ITX is very small. Motherboards must fit the case.
choices: The size standard of the case (ATX, micro-ATX, mini-ITX)

exercises.question: What should you do before touching internal components?
exercises.answer: Ground yourself to avoid static electricity damaging parts
exercises.explain: Static discharge can kill components. Touch a metal case part or wear an anti-static strap to discharge static electricity safely.
choices: Put on a wool sweater first
Ground yourself to avoid static electricity damaging parts

exercises.question: What is POST (Power-on Self Test)?
exercises.answer: A check the BIOS runs to verify hardware before booting the OS
exercises.explain: POST checks that the CPU, RAM, and other basics are working. If it fails, you may hear beep codes or see debug lights. If it passes, the OS starts loading.
choices: A check the BIOS runs to verify hardware before booting the OS
A way to turn off the computer

exercises.question: What does it mean if a computer beeps repeatedly on startup?
exercises.answer: The POST detected a hardware problem
exercises.explain: Beep patterns vary by maker, so check the board manual. Repeated beeps often point to RAM that is missing or not seated correctly.
choices: The POST detected a hardware problem

exercises.question: What is a sensible first step if a computer will not boot?
exercises.answer: Reseat RAM, check power connections, then try again
exercises.explain: Many boot failures are caused by loose connections. Reseat RAM (remove and reinstall), check all power plugs, then retry.
choices: Reseat RAM, check power connections, then try again

exercises.question: What are signs of a failing hard drive?
exercises.answer: Clicking sounds, slow file access, or frequent crashes
exercises.explain: A dying drive makes clicking sounds (mechanical failure), takes forever to open files, or crashes the system. Back up your data immediately.
choices: Clicking sounds, slow file access, or frequent crashes
The drive is always quiet when failing

exercises.question: What is a blue screen of death (BSOD)?
exercises.answer: A critical system error that forces a restart
exercises.explain: A BSOD indicates a serious problem such as a driver issue, hardware failure, or bad RAM. It shows an error code and restarts the PC. Newer Windows versions show a black screen instead.
choices: A critical system error that forces a restart
